claims.claim: AML.T0051 LLM Prompt Injection maps to tactic Execution (AML.TA0005); sub-techniques .000 Direct, .001 Indirect, .002 Triggered list no tactics of their own
AML.T0054 LLM Jailbreak maps to Privilege Escalation and Defense Evasion
AML.T0068 LLM Prompt Obfuscation is Defense Evasion; AML.T0077 LLM Response Rendering and AML.T0086 Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation are Exfiltration
Attackers refine attempts; detecting failed tool or API calls could identify earlier stages of an attack
ApiManagementGatewayLogs has columns ApimSubscriptionId, ApiId, OperationId, Url, CallerIpAddress, ResponseCode, CorrelationId, RequestBody, BackendRequestBody, BackendResponseBody, ResponseBody
ApiManagementGatewayLlmLog has DeploymentName, ModelName, PromptTokens, CompletionTokens, TotalTokens, RequestMessages, ResponseMessages, CorrelationId, SequenceNumber
Diagnostic categories are named 'Logs related to ApiManagement Gateway' and 'Logs related to generative AI gateway'
claims.locator: Azure Monitor-based dashboard steps and tip

NCSC advises logging potentially including full input and output of the LLM, tool use and API calls

claims.locator: Configure the Azure AI Content Safety API

claims.claim: Response fields userPromptAnalysis.attackDetected and documentsAnalysis[].attackDetected are Booleans, one result per document provided
The API does not itself block or route content; blocking, excluding or escalating requires application logic
Annotations return detected and filtered; user prompt attack annotation is prompt_filter_results[].content_filter_results.jailbreak
A filtered prompt returns HTTP 400 with error code content_filter
User prompt attack detection is enabled by default; document attack detection is off by default
Documents must be marked with the delimiter """ <documents> ... </documents> """ for indirect attack detection in the built-in filter
Prompt Shields is described as a probabilistic classifier-based approach
System prompts often include rules and examples that look like attacks, which causes false positives
False positive troubleshooting list: system prompt not in userPrompt or documents, block to annotate, review subtypes, consider exempting trusted input sources
A no-attack result does not establish that the document is trustworthy
claims.locator: Prompt Shields for documents, Examples table

claims.claim: Models are primarily trained and evaluated on English content; performance can vary for non-English
Prompt Shields do not determine whether content is harmful, accurate, or aligned with the application's task
OWASP scenarios include payload splitting, multilingual or obfuscated attacks and multimodal injection
NIST AI 600-1 action MS-2.7-007: perform AI red-teaming to assess resilience against GAI attacks (e.g., prompt injection)
NCSC advises against deny-listing known bad phrases because attackers can rephrase
Class names: Attempt to change system rules, Embedding a conversation mockup, Role-Play, Encoding Attacks; document classes include Information Gathering
Defender for Cloud alert 'ASCII Smuggling prompt injection detected' covers invisible instructions
Impacts listed by MSRC: markdown or HTML image (no user interaction), clickable link (needs click), tool calls, phishing from trusted sources, remote command execution
CVE-2025-32711: AI command injection in M365 Copilot allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network; CVSS 3.1 base 9.3
The model returns tool_calls items with id, type, function name and arguments; the application executes the function
JailbreakDetected is a boolean flag on Messages; XPIADetected is a boolean on AccessedResources denoting a cross prompt injection attack detected from a resource Copilot accessed
claims.locator: Common properties table, Messages and AccessedResources rows

claims.claim: Defender for Cloud AI threat protection works with Prompt Shields and threat intelligence and integrates with Defender XDR
Alert types and severities: Jailbreak BlockedAttempt Medium, DetectedAttempt Medium, ASCIISmuggling High, CredentialTheftAttempt Medium, MaliciousUrl.ModelResponse High, AnomalousToolInvocation Low
DetectedAttempt description: detected but not blocked due to content filtering settings or due to low confidence
Microsoft deterministically blocks known exfiltration methods such as markdown image injection
userPrompt holds user input and documents holds third-party content such as emails; response has userPromptAnalysis and documentsAnalysis with attackDetected
The Prompt Shields API does not block by itself; the application decides
Clean result does not establish the document is trustworthy; models primarily trained on English
Image exfiltration needs no user interaction, link needs a click, tool calls can leak directly
Completion body carries prompt_filter_results with content_filter_results.jailbreak detected and filtered
False positive advice: keep system prompt out, consider exempting trusted input sources, annotate mode logs without filtering
Chat completions path is /openai/deployments/{deployment-id}/chat/completions with an api-version parameter

quiz_map.support: Did instruction-like text arrive? | The input itself and a classifier verdict on it
default settings do not include details of requests or responses such as request or response bodies.
`documentsAnalysis`: a list with one `attackDetected` value for each document provided.
ensure the system prompt is not in `userPrompt` or `documents`
That is a report about an attack, and the real lead is the original email, not the ticket.
The request alone is still only an attempt.
When `XPIADetected` is true, the same entry gives you the pivot: `SiteUrl` and `Name` identify the file, page or email that carried the text.
The web proxy log for the staff member's workstation shows a GET request to `repairs-status-img.example` at 10:02:19, allowed, 14 seconds after the completion.
a list with one attackDetected value for each document provided
A true value under documentsAnalysis points at third-party content, which means an indirect attempt.
ApimSubscriptionId | Which application's subscription made the call
A verdict proves that attack-like text arrived. It does not prove that the model saw it or obeyed it.
When the content is a real attempt that was stopped, the rule worked: that is a true positive of low severity, worth recording because attackers refine and retry.
no document attack pattern detected does not establish that the document is trustworthy.
When the content is not an attack at all, the rule misfired and the verdict is false positive.
An attempt stops at the first or second stage. A success reaches the third, and an incident is confirmed at the fourth or fifth.
A confirmed outside effect is a true positive and an incident, even when the classifier said false.
Work in this order, because each step tells you where to look next.
Exempt narrowly: one verified, expected source, never a phrase and never the whole application.
The address inside the image markup names the host that receives the data.
